question: Are the current execution and mechanism_next artifacts sufficient and closed for exactly one controlled two-task table, one neighborhood figure, one realized-future figure, two primary claims, and the chain shaping -> lower F -> larger radius -> less damage?

review.integrity_note: No scope-matched EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.json was found; this does not block the provisional judgment.

scope.primary_current_regime: ImageNet-A, ViT-B/16, Q/V LoRA rank 10, training seed 0
scope.legacy_regime_kept_separate: ImageNet-R, fresh K/V LoRA, Adam, seeds 0/1/2, batch-gradient Fisher proxy

overall.what_results_support: A one-seed, coordinate-specific result: the GAM anchor has lower train256 raw empirical-Fisher and lower sampled train damage; both realized directions yield lower D_test on the GAM anchor at all ten nonzero anchor-matched cells; and the historical GAM-to-GAM chain has lower Task0 damage despite larger displacement, with lower Task0-to-Task9 endpoint-chord directional sensitivity.
overall.what_results_dont_support: The current data do not support a split-robust lower-neighborhood-damage claim, a generally larger tolerated radius, a worst-case neighborhood guarantee, a causal mediation chain, an optimizer-trajectory sensitivity claim, or a cross-seed/cross-dataset general claim.
missing_evidence: test307 raw per-example Fisher on the predeclared sparse radii
a genuine finite sensitivity-directed search and cross-anchor evaluation
Task1 and Task5 endpoint-chord path sensitivities under the same protocol as Task9
a predeclared dense loss-only radius grid only if the larger-radius claim is retained
matching seeds 1/2 only if a cross-seed formal claim is retained
overall.suggested_claim_revision: In one ImageNet-A seed of the current visual GAM+EWC implementation, the GAM Task0 anchor has lower raw empirical-Fisher and lower sampled train-neighborhood damage in fixed effective-Q/V coordinates, but not lower test mean positive damage or a larger current G-tolerance radius. Along two realized directions it has lower finite-displacement test damage; separately, the historical full GAM-to-GAM sequence reaches Task9 with lower old-task damage and lower endpoint-chord directional sensitivity despite larger displacement. These are direction- and coordinate-dependent descriptive observations, not a complete causal chain.
overall.next_experiments_needed: For the narrow case, none; only reporting corrections are required. For the attachment's broad chain, run the small test-raw-Fisher and directed-probe diagnostics, add t1/t5 chords, and either measure the larger-radius arrow with a predeclared loss-only grid or delete that arrow.

design.reason: The two claims, A/B/C roles, and one-table/two-figure structure are explicit and coherent.

implementation.reason: Existing seed0 measurement/rendering code is implemented, and an 88-job full_rq2 formal plan exists, but mechanism_next follow-ups remain proposed_not_queued; the formal queue has no state, full_rq2 sparse-test omits r=5 by default, its path sample scope differs from existing t9, and bridge_full does not implement sensitivity-directed search.

execution.reason: Seed0 A/B/C, the 2x2 realized-direction bridge, all ten task endpoints, and the t9 chord are complete. Test raw Fisher, directed search, t1/t5 chords, and formal matching multi-seed results are absent. At the snapshot the formal queue had no state and zero complete training receipts; two completed micro-smokes are code checks only, while the replacement lambda=0 pilot was still running.

semantic.reason: Test G reverses at all six nonzero radii and the reported G tolerance radii tie, so the full chain breaks before the larger-radius node.

primary_claims.claim: Shaping lowers neighborhood Fisher sensitivity and enlarges the damage-tolerant region.
primary_claims.what_results_support: On train256, GAM/SGD raw-trace ratios are 0.468-0.520 over the measured radii, and train G/Q95 are lower at all six nonzero radii.
primary_claims.what_results_dont_support: Test raw Fisher is unmeasured; test G is higher at all six nonzero radii; train and test G prefix-safe radii tie for every reported epsilon, and test Q95 radii also tie.
primary_claims.suggested_claim_revision: The seed0 GAM anchor has lower sampled train-neighborhood empirical-gradient sensitivity; no split-robust or larger-radius claim is made.

primary_claims.claim: Lower directional sensitivity allows realized future drift to cause less old-task damage.
primary_claims.what_results_support: At Task9, GAM-to-GAM has drift 1.400472589 versus 1.197584100, test damage 0.034347380 versus 0.260130529, and endpoint-chord S_path 0.014793093 versus 0.368057602. GAM-to-GAM also has greater drift and lower test damage at every Task1-Task9 endpoint.
primary_claims.what_results_dont_support: Only the Task9 ambient endpoint chord was integrated; it is not the optimizer path, and the compared full sequences use different future optimizers. Causal mediation is not identified.
primary_claims.suggested_claim_revision: Lower endpoint-chord sensitivity is associated with lower realized damage despite larger displacement in this seed0 historical full-sequence comparison.

arrow_status.evidence: Current ImageNet-A raw trace is 1465.496927 vs 761.900774 at the anchors and 2008.387873 vs 940.412532 after common SGD+EWC continuation.
G prefix-safe radii tie on train and test for every reported epsilon; test G is worse for GAM at 6/6 nonzero radii.
The larger-radius premise is not observed, and radius was not independently intervened on.

arrow_status.arrow: lower realized-direction/chord sensitivity <-> less realized damage despite larger drift
arrow_status.evidence: GAM anchor D_test is lower in 10/10 nonzero cross-anchor bridge comparisons; Task9 S_path and damage are lower while displacement is larger. Direction effects are strong and the evidence is single-seed association.

A_current_imageneta.interpretation: The inherited package changes and raw trace is lower, but current class-IL retention/plasticity does not improve. T1 trace exists in CSV and can be added to the rendered table without training.

limitations: Different dataset, optimizer, parameter lifecycle, and Fisher estimator from current ImageNet-A B/C.
F2 proxy and endpoint base loss are on the new-task classes, not an old-task endpoint D1.
All 18 logs have save_ckp=False, so old-task D1 cannot be added from existing checkpoints.

B_random.G_tolerance_radius: ties for both methods at every reported epsilon on train and test
B_random.test_Q95_tolerance_radius: ties for both methods at every reported epsilon

B_bridge.limitation: The two realized directions are finite probes, not sensitivity-directed raw-Fisher searches or worst-case certificates.

C.all_tasks_checkpoint_coverage: Task0 through Task9 for both historical full chains
C.limitation: GAM-to-GAM is distinct from A's GAM-anchor-to-SGD continuation.

attachment_full_chain: Do not retrain or expand A by default; add existing T1 raw trace to the current table. If the legacy ImageNet-R table requires D1, retrain only that exact pair; otherwise omit D1 with a scope note.
Run test307 raw per-example Fisher for both anchors at r={0,1,5,10,20} with the existing paired directions.
Implement and run one fixed-budget sensitivity-directed finite probe per source anchor on an independent train calibration subset, then cross-evaluate both directions on both anchors.
If and only if the larger-radius wording is retained, run a common predeclared dense loss-only radius grid; remove the arrow if it remains null or negative.
Compute Task1 and Task5 endpoint chords under the same data/coordinate/integration protocol as Task9.
Add matching seeds 1/2 only for a formal cross-seed claim after the protocol is frozen.
narrow_direction_dependent_case: Add existing T1 raw trace to the current A table and retain the unfavorable a21/a22 result.
Retain negative/neutral random-neighborhood and tolerance results in Figure B; remove general larger-radius and worst-case wording.
Label C's Fisher quantity endpoint-segment sensitivity, show that only Task9 is measured, and keep A GAM-to-SGD separate from C GAM-to-GAM.

a promise that additional experiments will produce a positive sign
